action_args.justification: The series has a strong downward trend (slope agreement 0.98) and strong weekly seasonality (period 52, residual corr 0.71), making it highly predictable. Model ranking is unstable across the 3 validation windows (Kendall tau -0.029, no model is always top-3), so no subset or fitted weighting can reliably outperform a broad average. The full-pool mean (19 models) is the best strategy tested and the runner-up (median) is not statistically distinguishable. The correlated-error structure (10 groups, 5 independent) means the full pool still captures complementary signal across wavelet-transformed RF, catboost, and classical models, and trimming or pruning only removes that diversity. Accepting the robust full-pool mean is consistent with the series' mixed-regime, high-predictability character.

3. **Diagnosis**: Mixed regime, high predictability, robust combination hint, unstable ranking, correlated errors, only 3 validation windows (high variance in weight estimation)

- The ranking is unstable (Kendall tau -0.029), which means no single model or small subset is reliably best
- There are 5 redundant groups of correlated errors, meaning many models are essentially saying the same thing
- The full pool mean (a1) is the best so far, beating the median (a2) and all subset-based strategies
- The dataset card shows that median and trimmed_mean strategies tend to work well on other series
- The diagnosis says "robust" combination is favored
- Only 3 validation windows means weight estimation is high variance
